resolutions: Any well-formed typed verbstem remains open input; Canvas examples do not form a stem whitelist.
The user chooses the intended Source Valence rather than having it inferred from the final vowel.
Final i and a tendencies are concise reading cues with genuine exceptions.
Final o may reflect a nonactive result, and hua plus a/e shapes remain readable without becoming admission rules.
The same stem shape may carry distinct intransitive and transitive Source analyses when the intended lexical analysis permits it.
A transitive analysis requires its real object participant.
No valence-neutral toggle, meaning-family switch, example picker, or stored-stem selector is added.
Later passive or impersonal formation follows the already selected typed Valence.
An open final-i intransitive Source receives productive Type 1 causative analysis without stored-stem authorization.
Replacement removes final i and adds short causative a.
Addition preserves final i and adds long causative ā.
Replacement produces Class B and addition produces Class C automatically.
The Source subject becomes the causative object and the new outer subject is imported automatically.
Replacement versus addition is a user choice only when both remain valid for the typed Source analysis.
A Source whose canonical analysis fixes one procedure does not receive a redundant procedure choice.
A special consonant alternation is used only when the intended canonical lexical analysis requires it.
Vowel quantity, target class, participant transfer, meaning notes, and example identity are not separate controls.
Clickable cues expose final-vowel evidence, typed Valence consequences, and the selected causative boundary without authorizing grammar from display text.
Ordinary final-a causatives replace source a morphologically even when source and target spelling are identical.
Ordinary final-a replacement automatically yields a Class B causative.
A typed root-plus-ya Source normally loses ya and receives long causative ā.
Normal root-plus-ya replacement automatically yields a Class C causative.
Retained y is preserved only for a licensed lexical exception rather than offered universally.
The user never chooses visible replacement, vowel length, target class, or example identity separately.
A destockal Source analysis preserves ordered root, stock formative, and stem formative.
Root plus stock formative forms the stock; adding the theme forms the completed verbstem.
The intermediate stock is not presented as the completed destockal VNC Source.
Entered boundaries remain part of the canonical Source formula and do not become separate slots.
Any open long-vowel ni or hui Source can receive the typed destockal analysis without inventory admission.
The long stock vowel and ni or hui theme are derived from the typed Source segmentation.
Regular stock-vowel harmony is computed from the last root vowel as a cue rather than an admission rule.
An exceptional stock vowel remains authorized when that typed analysis is genuinely intended.
Only an exceptional stock-vowel analysis carries an additional confirmation need.
The completed ni or hui Source is projected through its typed Class B machinery.
Productivity notes, lexical meanings, perfectives, and Canvas inventories remain reading evidence.
Clickable cues keep root-stock-stem rank, harmony or exception, and Source class visible without creating grammar authority.
Open ni and hui destockal Sources can use replacement or addition without stored-stem admission.
Replacement versus addition is shown only when both procedures remain valid for the typed destockal Source.
Destockal replacement changes final i to short causative a and derives Class B.
Destockal addition preserves the Source, adds long causative ā, and derives Class C.
Majority preferences and named exceptions remain cues rather than grammar authority.
Destockal causative target structure and participant transfer are automatic after the procedure is selected.
An underlying root-stock vowel boundary remains separate in the formula.
Identical root and stock vowels coalesce only in the written projection.
Any open segmented Source can receive the coalescence rule without example-list admission.
A reconstructed or obsolete Source history is supplied only when that is the user's intended Source analysis.
The typed underlying analysis and its provenance remain attached through later causative formation.
Coalescence, double vowels, asterisks, obsolete status, and example identity are not separate controls.
Open ā-hua and ē-hua destockal Sources are accepted without a stem whitelist.
Independently entered hua and hui synonyms remain separate lexical Sources.
Type 1 hua causatives automatically replace hua with hu-a.
Hua replacement automatically derives a Class B target.
Destockal, compound, exceptional-class, or reconstructed confirmation appears only for genuine Source ambiguity.
Hua meanings, nounroot resemblances, dictionary gaps, and examples remain reading evidence.
Open i-hui, a-hui, and o-hui Sources are accepted without a stem whitelist.
For short hui Sources, the last root vowel derives the regular short stock cue.
A root ending in l selects short i and overrides the ordinary root-vowel cue.
A genuinely exceptional short stock analysis is confirmed rather than silently normalized.
Regular i-hui and a-hui causatives replace the full ending with o-ā.
Special o-hui causatives replace hui with ā while preserving source o.
Short hui causatives derive a Class C target from a Class B Source.
Exact missing counterparts remain blocked only for their exact typed Source relation.
The irregular pil-ca to pil-o-ā relation remains distinct from pil-i-hui and does not create a productive ca rule.
Stock-vowel conditions, replacement material, classes, gaps, and example identity are not separate controls.
The user chooses the imported causative subject.
An active Source subject becomes the causative object automatically.
An impersonal Source agent becomes a nonspecific causative object automatically.
A referentially empty impersonal surface subject is discarded during participant transfer.
The causative governs the newly added object while preserving the complete Source VNC core.
Different source and target persons derive a specific projective causee without another choice.
Matching first-person source and target categories derive reflexive causee structure automatically.
Matching non-first-person categories expose projective versus reflexive only because both typed interpretations remain valid.
Specific or nonspecific carrier, governor, formula line, and translation wording remain derived facts.
Clickable participant cues expose Source voice, transfer, imported subject, and genuine or automatic coreference without authorizing grammar from display text.
